title: "General Rules"

Let's pull everything from this tutorial together into a short, reusable reference.

## General Rules for Calling Functions

1. A function call always follows the pattern `function_name(arguments)`.
1. Every opening parenthesis needs a matching closing parenthesis.
1. Function names (and argument names) are case-sensitive: `mean()` and `Mean()` are not the same thing.
1. Arguments are separated by commas.
1. You can name arguments (`round(x = 3.14159, digits = 2)`) or rely on their order (`round(3.14159, 2)`), but if you
   skip a name, the order matters.
1. Text values must be wrapped in quotes (`"like this"`); object names and numbers are not.

## Practice

Using what you've learned across this tutorial, write a single R expression that:

1. Creates a vector of the numbers 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, and 42, called `nums`.
1. Calculates the mean of `nums`, rounded to 1 decimal place.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
## {{< var tab_title.editor >}}

```{webr-r}
```

## {{< var tab_title.hint >}}

You'll need three functions here: one to build the vector, one to average it, and one to round the result. You've used
all three earlier in this tutorial.

## {{< var tab_title.solution >}}

```{r}
nums <- c(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42)
round(mean(nums), 1)
```

Notice that this solution *nests* one function call inside another: `mean(nums)` is calculated first, and its result
is immediately passed as the input to `round()`. You'll see this pattern constantly once you get comfortable with it.
